Hi Danielle —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is BrightWave_SOW_v3.pdf which reflects the ramp you outlined (Q1: 20% reserved, Q2: 40%, Q3+: 100%), plus the pricing worksheet. Two quick items I want to call out before we route to procurement:

- Auto-renew language: our standard is an automatic annual renewal unless either party gives 60 days' notice. I wanted to confirm whether BrightWave needs an opt-out/escape clause tied to a quarterly usage review (you mentioned internal budgeting windows).
- Co-terming: we can either keep your two product lines on independent anniversaries or co-term into a single renewal date to simplify billing. Co-terming usually requires a short pro-rated bridge period.

Can you confirm which path procurement prefers? If you want co-terming we’ll propose a 90-day bridge to align with your fiscal year.

Thanks — I’m looping Marissa for pricing sign-off.

Best,
Rachel

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the SOW. Procurement wants two items clarified before they advance to legal: 1) they want an escape clause that permits them to exit the auto-renew if average utilization across any two consecutive quarters falls below 30% of committed capacity, with a 60-day notice; and 2) billing cadence — they'd prefer annualized billing rather than monthly invoicing tied to usage.

We’re leaning towards co-terming both product lines onto our fiscal anniversary (Jan 1). Would a 4-month bridge be possible to align on Jan? If co-terming increases first-year spend materially, I’ll need to flag to finance for approval.

Thanks — Danielle

Hi Danielle / Procurement team —

Thanks for the clear feedback. Quick responses inline: 1) Escape clause: we can include a utilization-triggered opt-out (two consecutive quarters <30%) with 60 days' notice, but we need to add a minimum termination fee equal to 10% of remaining committed dollars in the current term to cover reserved capacity provisioning. 2) Billing cadence: we can offer annualized billing with a one-time invoice at start of term (or quarterly invoices if you prefer smoothing).

On co-terming: co-term to Jan 1 with a 4-month bridge is doable. To smooth P&L impact we can propose a pro-rated credit in month 1 of the new term (equivalent to unused bridge months) or offer to front-load a 30% onboarding credit applied to first billing quarter. I’ve included Marissa and Karthik to confirm pricing/credit mechanics.

If procurement is okay with the termination fee and the annual invoice, I’ll issue an updated SOW and DocuSign packet for signature.

Best,
Rachel

Subject: Re: Draft SOW + a quick question on auto-renew

Thanks for looping me in — quick proposal from an ops/serving perspective to limit friction and protect unit economics:

- Bridge structure: 4-month bridge that ramps 25% increments (month 1: 25% reserved, month 2: 50%, month 3: 75%, month 4: 100%). That gives BrightWave predictable onramps and keeps the first full calendar year aligned with Jan 1 co-term.
- Escape clause mechanics: allow the utilization-triggered opt-out but require a 10% termination fee as Rachel proposed OR a 2-quarter reconciliation true-up that would convert reserved credit into overage credits if utilization is low. This provides finance-friendly alternatives.
- Billing: annual invoice but we can include an interstitial invoice for the bridge period only (short pro-rated invoice) to avoid a large one-off. Alternatively, apply the onboarding credit to offset the bridge invoice.

I think this balances BrightWave's request for an exit path with our need to reserve capacity. If that works I’ll ask legal to bake in the exact trigger language and we can prepare a DocuSign envelope.

Karthik
